title: Unbounded Recursion on Nested Structs
pattern: Recursive function definitions that process nested structural elements (such as syntax trees, linked lists, or directory hierarchies) without bounding traversal depth or using safe heap-based stacks.
why_bad: Every recursive function call allocates a new frame on the thread's stack [316]. Stack size is strictly bounded (typically 2-8MB). Traversing deeply nested or cyclic inputs (which can be crafted by attackers or generated by bad files) will rapidly exhaust the stack limit, causing an immediate, unrecoverable stack overflow crash [316, 324].
detection: Identify self-invoking recursive functions processing structural data fields (such as `Box<Self>` or tree children) without tracking depth limits.
fix: Refactor recursive methods to use iterative loops with a heap-allocated `Vec` stack, or enforce a strict recursive depth check threshold [316, 324].
source: Benjamin C. Pierce, *Types and Programming Languages*, Chapter 21 / passage [316]; Chlipala A, *Certified programming with dependent types*, Chapter 6 / passage [324].
